convoLines.text: "My cut needs a second pair of hands. Will you help me clean it?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Morris is gone, Sam is gone, and Petra is gone. The fire doesn't care. That's what gets me — the fire doesn't care."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
"Here. I made an extra." Tao presses something into your hand — a decent tool, oiled and kept. (Useful. Keep it.)
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Tao grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Tao is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"I memorize the stars. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
They spread their hands, smiling — the words are missing, but the meaning lands anyway.
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
They answer at length. They nod back, slowly.
They answer at length. A grin breaks through, quick and warm. "Water?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
They answer at length. You press a hand to your own chest, then point at them. Together — they get it.
A final shared look — you both feel the talk running its course.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can we talk?" Tao sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
You can feel the history in how they greet you.
"About this wound — I hate to ask twice, but it's still open. Will you?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "I dreamed Morris was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Tao is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"I'm picking up Morris's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"This was good." They mean it.
They spread their hands, smiling — the words are missing, but the meaning lands anyway.
"Yeah? What's up?"
They answer at length. They nod back, a little quicker this time.
They answer at length. A smile, tired but real.
They answer at length. You point at yourself, then at them, then at the fire. Together. They get it.
They glance toward their own thoughts; the exchange is winding down.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can we talk?" Tao glances around first. "People are saying things. About you. Is any of it true?"
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"About this wound — the need hasn't gone anywhere. I'm still asking."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"

"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Have you heard what they're calling Static? I'm pushing 'Big Big'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"Okay. Thank you for telling me."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Tao is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening. That's still where we are."
"Anyway — I should get going."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
They speak. You understand none of it. "Water?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
They spread their hands, smiling — the words are missing, but the meaning lands anyway.
"Yeah? What's up? Gotta keep moving."
They answer at length. They smile back, slower this time, like it just landed.
A gesture, patient and clear: palms up, then toward you.
They glance toward their own thoughts; the exchange is winding down.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.

lines: d23: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Morris Wilson is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d23: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d23: 🕯️ Morris Wilson is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d23: What Morris kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d23: "Morris's gone." Tao looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Morris." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d23: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Aaron blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d23: 📖 LEARNED: Reading Tracks (Level 1). Fresh tracks have sharp edges. Old tracks crumble. You can tell how recently something passed.
d23: 📖 LEARNED: Patient Aim (Level 1). One shot. You don't take the shot unless it's the shot.
d23: 📖 LEARNED: Animal Behavior (Level 1). Most animals flee. Give them an escape route and they take it. Cornered animals fight.
d23: 📖 LEARNED: Wire Snares (Level 1). A loop of wire on a game trail. Simple, effective, ancient. Check at dawn.

d23: 📖 LEARNED: Come Get Some (Level 1). Make exactly the right noise and the blind thing comes to investigate. Goad a blinded monster within 3 tiles: it lurches toward the sound on its next move. Stand where you want it.
d23: 📖 LEARNED: Scarecrow (Level 1). You can stage a fake injury to lure monsters into traps. They fall for it. Every time.
d23: 📖 LEARNED: Soft Step (Level 1). Move through woods like weather. Less noise, fewer surprises.
d23: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d23: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Morris Wilson, 23 days. The mantle passes to Aaron Gallo.
d23: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Aaron Gallo, 42 — a hunting guide. Their hands know different work now: Beast-calm, Echo Location.
d23: The village's quarrel was with Morris — and Morris is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d23: At the grave, Tao, Sam, Tariq speak for Aaron — "Morris trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d23: The fire knew Aaron before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.

d38: 💀 Simon starved. Slowly. Somebody's sleeping-roll stays rolled out. Nobody puts it away.
d38: ⚠ Haven's pantry is empty. Day 3 of hunger.
d38: Haven couldn't hold. On the third hungry day, people started walking — in different directions. The scattering, again.
d38: Arturo spent the afternoon at the workbench, and the Arrow came apart in their hands. The materials are wasted.
